steps.text: Place the cabbage in a large bowl, cover, and place in the refrigerator to chill for 30 minutes. Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat, and cook and stir the ramen noodles, sesame seeds, and almonds until lightly browned; set aside to cool.
Prepare the dressing by mixing the canola oil, soy sauce, sugar, balsamic, and white vinegars in a blender until smooth.
About 30 minutes before serving, toss the dressing and cabbage mixture together; chill. Just before serving, toss the noodle mixture with the cabbage mixture.

raw_recipe.headline: Napa Cabbage Noodle Salad
raw_recipe.description: A delicious napa cabbage salad with lots of crunchy noodles and almonds tossed in a sweet and tangy vinegar-soy dressing.

review.reviewBody: Hi I added a can of drained mandrin orange slices Ummm good

We have tried various versions of this type salad and loved them all but this seems to have way too much oil. 1 and 1/2 total when almost none is needed. Dry roast the crunchies in nonstick pan and cut back on the sugar and add dressing as needed if your head of napa is not very large. I did a side of grilled chicken strips which added to the meal.
This is pretty much the same as an old recipe I used for years (that I misplaced). I added about 1/2 cup chopped green onions and some shredded chicken. Very good the next day.

Ate a wonderful version of this at a BSF fellowship luncheon yesterday and all the ladies raved and begged for the recipe! I didn't want to wait until next week and found this one on allricpes. She served the cabbage, crunchies and dressing seperately. The crunchies she used was ramen noodles, sliced almonds, salted sunflower seeds and sasame seeds. The dressing was also similiar except she said she added the seasoning packet from the asian ramen noodles. I made this at home tonight and it was great! (Didn't bake crunchies in oven-didn't need it).

Very good, but can be made much healthier than as written. I toasted the almonds & ramen noodles without any oil, and they turned out just fine. Also cut down on the amount of sugar & oil in the dressing, and added julliened red peppers and chopped green onions to the napa cabbage. I keep everything separate until serving, since the cabbage gets soggy pretty quickly. Keeping everything separate also improves the quality of leftovers, and this recipe makes quite a lot, so unless you're taking it to a party, you may be eating it for several days.
I add a tablespoon of mayonnaise to the sauce. I also add 1 box of penne pasta. Two tablespoons of Siracha sauce. I haven't had a complaint yet. In fact I always get asked for the recipe at parties.

Salads like this have always been a favorite of mine. But I was "afraid" to mix the amount of olive oil into the cabbage that the recipe called for because I thought it would make the entire salad too oily. So instead, I toasted the ramen noodles, almonds, and sesame seeds in a skillet before combining with the cabbage and the dressing. Also saved some of the ramen noodles for a garnish on top and added some leftover chicken for a complete, quick meal.

This is a terrific salad. I didn't make this version, but I can tell you what I do a bit different with mine. Instead of canola oil, cook the noodles, seeds, and almonds in 1/4 C. salted butter. When browned, pour out onto a paper towel to cool. I also add chopped green chives. You can also use pecans instead of almonds. Love this salad!

I like to marinate chicken in some of the dressing, grill it and chop it up and add to the salad. 
This is one of my favorite salads! :-)

I've made this twice now and I think I made a good mistake the first time.....I cooked the noodles, nuts and seeds in a dry pan (no oil added). For my second time I added oil to the pan (about half what the recipe calls for) and found the noodles etc were way too oily.
The dressing is delicious as is!

Fabulous salad. I used granulated Splenda in place of sugar and added some roasted salted sunflower seeds. But the biggie: My son got out the sriracha hot chili sauce to put on top of his. He raved about how good it was, so I did the same. That put it over the top. A perfect addition for those who like spicy. I would suggest adding 2-3 T of this to the dressing. You will love it.

Very good as written. Made 1/4 recipe to try and made 4 medium side servings. Amount of dressing seemed small but was plenty. Tasted good but wanted some color so will experiment with peppers, etc next time.
it turned out awesome ill be adding tha tot my list of big dinners
I loved this salad, I didn't have almond slivers so I used pecans and it was awesome!
I made it yesterday for a family get together & it was a hit. I plan to make it again.

I used savoy cabbage, half a head...didn't realize it would shrink so much; used all olive oil, no canola; I used Swerve and honey for sweetener; I did not use the noodles, used peanuts instead of almonds; I didn't use measuring spoons cuz I'm adventurous like that ha ha...sooo it was too vinegary and because of that I added some avocado mayo which made it the bomb!!! Also used some spices, salt pepper garlic onion cayenne. So so good, def in my favorites:)
Too sweet.

02.05.17 ~ Made this salad for one of the MANY items we had at our Super Bowl party. It was very good and well received. Next time I'm going to add a little shaved carrot for color. Once I made the original recipe, I split it in to two bowls and added green onions to one of the bowls. I preferred the bowl with the onions, although both were delicious.
I recommended cutting down on the sugar, I used a small head of napa cabbage, great flavors but a bit too sweet.
Delicious. Makes enough for about 8 regular sized servings.
